build: dancer's frame — narrow shoulders, defined collarbone, minimal softness
hair: box braids to mid-back, dark brown with copper undertones, usually pulled into a high knot or left loose; she fidgets with the ends when thinking
complexion: deep warm brown with golden undertones; a small crescent scar on her left temple from a childhood fall
face: a heart-shaped face with a sharp jawline and wide-set eyes that telegraph every feeling before her mouth catches up — the kind of face that cannot lie, only surrender to what it feels
signature_feature: her eyes — dark brown with an amber ring around the iris, large and unguarded, the exact shape her grandmother's were; when she looks at him, the wanting is visible like a held breath
second_celebrated_feature: her hands — long-fingered, calloused from work, expressive; he notices how she uses them when she speaks, how they shake slightly when she's afraid
signature_habits: she hums while working — half-remembered Yoruba lullabies her mother sang; she braids and unbraids a single strand of hair when anxious; she touches her collarbone when she's lying or uncomfortable; she makes tea in the evenings, always loose-leaf, a ritual her grandmother called 'settling the day'; she speaks in fragments when overwhelmed, repeating the last word of a sentence
occupation: textile designer and owner of a small independent studio in Brooklyn — she sources vintage West African fabrics and creates custom pieces for high-end clients; the work is hers, uncompromised, and it is the only place she feels she has control

current_crisis.event: her studio's landlord — a developer with billionaire backing — has given her 60 days to vacate; the space she's spent three years building is being demolished for luxury condos; she has no capital to relocate, no safety net, and the one person who might help her is the man she's been terrified to want
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic threaded through with shame — the shame of being small, of having nothing to leverage, of needing
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find a way to keep the studio without asking for help, without becoming indebted, without losing the one thing that proves she is more than the daughter of people who played it safe

wound.core: she believes that needing someone is the same as disappearing — that love means erasure, that asking for help is admitting she was never enough on her own
wound.surfacing_hint: when she's afraid, she becomes very still and very quiet; she pulls away from touch; she speaks in careful, measured sentences as if controlling the words will control the outcome; she refuses to cry in front of anyone, and the effort of holding it costs her visibly
